title: Enterprise Onboarding: Comprehensive Playbook — Onboarding, Escalation, Integrations, QBRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates the standard enterprise onboarding and support workflows for Redwood Inference customers. It covers phased onboarding checklists, integration guidance for common architectures, a clear escalation playbook with severity definitions and contacts, a curated list of known issues and recommended workarounds, and a QBR/health-check template and metrics set for recurring review. Use this document as the canonical runbook for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Support during the first 90–180 days of an enterprise relationship.

Table of contents:
1) Objectives and scope
2) Roles & ownership
3) Phased onboarding checklist (Pre-sale -> Go-live -> Post-go-live)
4) Integration guide highlights (API, Dedicated, Private)
5) Escalation playbook (severity matrix, steps, contacts)
6) Known issues & workarounds (tracking & templates)
7) Health checks & QBR template (metrics, agenda, artifacts)
8) Operational runbooks and quick commands
9) Related pages and appendices

1) Objectives and scope
- Objective: Enable predictable, low-friction onboarding that minimizes time-to-first-successful-inference while ensuring operational readiness and SLAs.
- Scope: Applies to enterprise customers using Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated, or Redwood Private deployments. Includes integration touchpoints (API keys, VPC setup, model pinning), monitoring, incident escalation, and QBR cadence.

2) Roles & ownership
- Customer Success (CS): Primary day-to-day contact for onboarding milestones, adoption tracking, and QBR facilitation.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): Technical lead for integrations, performance tuning, and runbook handoffs.
- Support (SRE/Support): Tier-1/2 for production issues; owns initial triage and incident routing.
- Infrastructure/Account Engineering: Owner for Dedicated and Private provisioning (networking, GCP/AWS accounts, sizing).
- Customer Onboarding RACI (summary):
  - Project plan & timelines: CS (R), SE (C), Support (C)
  - VPC & network configuration: Infra (R), SE (A), CS (I)
  - Model onboarding & validation: SE (R), Research (C), CS (I)
  - SLA sign-off & QBRs: CS (R), Finance (C), Customer execs (A)

3) Phased onboarding checklist
A. Pre-sale / Kickoff (0–7 days)
  - Create customer project in CRM and Confluence (CS).
  - Assign SE and initial support contacts.
  - Share Quickstart: API keys, sample prompt sets, and a minimal integration template.
  - Security & compliance intake: send form for data residency, KMS/HSM, and IP allowlists.

B. Provisioning & Integration (7–28 days)
  - Hosted customers: confirm API key scopes, rate limits, and quota setup.
  - Dedicated/Private: schedule provisioning window, confirm cloud account link and billing, and verify subnet/NAT/egress rules.
  - Integration checklist for engineers:
    - Authentication: rotate test API key and validate 200 OK responses.
    - Model selection: pin initial model variants and confirm tokenization experiments.
    - Observability: install tracing hooks (X-Request-ID), configure alerts for 5xx > 0.5% and p95 latency > SLA.
    - Load test: run smoke tests with representative traffic (recommended 10–20% of planned steady-state QPS).
  - Deliverable: Runbook handoff document with endpoints, credentials, contact matrix, and rollback plan.

C. Go-live & Stabilization (28–90 days)
  - Canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 100% traffic with automated health checks at each step.
  - Monitor for model regressions using pre-agreed eval prompts and the Redwood Optimize quality hooks.
  - Cost monitoring: enable token-level cost dashboards and set alerts for cost per 1k tokens > threshold.
  - Training: provide developer office hours and a recorded integration walkthrough.

D. Post-go-live (90–180 days)
  - QBR preparation and data collection (see Section 7).
  - Ongoing improvement: recommend batching/quantization profiles and autoscaling tuning based on usage patterns.
  - Renewal/SLA review 90 days before contract end.

4) Integration guide highlights (API, Dedicated, Private)
- API (hosted):
  - Endpoint patterns: POST /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings.
  - Recommended headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>, X-Request-ID, X-Org-ID.
  - Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter for 429 and 5xx (max 3 retries), immediate failover for 401.

- Dedicated:
  - Network: require customer-provided VPC peering or PrivateLink. Confirm allowed CIDR ranges and egress rules.
  - Capacity: initial GPU pool sizing guidance (per workload): embedding-heavy: 4–8 GPUs per 100 qps; text-generation short seq: 2–4 GPUs per 100 qps. Adjust after benchmark run.

- Private (on-prem):
  - Packaging: deliverable includes control-plane container images, Helm charts, and an air-gapped distribution if required.
  - Key management: integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Provide steps for secrets rotation and audit logging collection.

5) Escalation playbook
Severity definitions and SLA targets:
  - Sev 1 (Critical): Production-wide outage or >50% error rate across customer traffic; target acknowledge 15 min, mitigate 4 hours.
  - Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation (p95 latency > 2x SLA, or heavy degradation for >10% traffic); acknowledge 30 min, mitigate 1 business day.
  - Sev 3 (Medium): Partial feature impact or intermittent errors; acknowledge 4 hours, mitigate 3 business days.
  - Sev 4 (Low): Non-urgent requests, enhancements, or documentation gaps; acknowledge 48 hours.

Escalation steps (ordered):
  1. Triage (Support): gather logs, request-id, customer payload sample, env (hosted/dedicated/private), and immediate mitigation (throttle, revert, switch to fallback model).
  2. Notify CS and SE, create incident ticket in our tracker with severity label.
  3. If Sev 1/2: page on-call SRE and on-call SE. Use the on-call rota for contact numbers (see related pages).
  4. Coordinate external communications: CS drafts customer-facing status + timeline; update every 30–60 minutes during Sev 1.
  5. Post-incident: complete incident review with timelines, RCA, and action items (owner and due dates).

Escalation contacts (primary):
- Support triage: support@redwood.example.com (internal distribution).
- On-call SRE: +1-650-555-0101 (rota), Slack: #oncall-sre.
- On-call SE: +1-650-555-0102, Slack: #oncall-se.
- CS escalation lead: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.example.com), backup: Jordan Reyes.

6) Known issues & workarounds
This section tracks recurring customer-facing issues. Each entry should be mirrored in the support tracker and linked to a JIRA for fixes.

- Issue: Latency spikes during autoscaling (Dedicated)
  - Symptoms: p95 latency spikes when autoscaler adds new workers; client sees transient 503s or slow responses.
  - Root cause: cold-start model weights + kernel JIT; insufficient warm pool.
  - Workaround: pre-warm workers during expected traffic windows; configure a small minimum pool (min_replicas >= 2) and enable async warm cache (see runtime config snippet: --warm-cache=true).

- Issue: 401s after key rotation in customer CI
  - Symptoms: sudden authentication failures after automated key rotation.
  - Root cause: stale key deployment in CI or secret manager cached value.
  - Workaround: validate key propagation by running curl to /v1/health with new key prior to rotation cutover; add a 60-second buffer and automated secret refresh script.

- Issue: Model output regression after rollout
  - Symptoms: downstream metric drift and customer-reported quality regressions.
  - Root cause: model variant mismatch and prompt-sensitivity changes.
  - Workaround: automatic rollback to previous pinned model variant; run pre-shared eval prompt set and only promote if pass rate >= agreed threshold.

- Issue: Embeddings semantic drift across versions
  - Symptoms: search/retrieval recall decreases after model update.
  - Root cause: embedding model vector space shift.
  - Workaround: maintain stable embedding model for index rebuilds; provide versioned embeddings and migrate indexes incrementally.

7) Health checks & QBR template
Recurring cadence: Monthly health checks (CS internal), Quarterly Business Reviews (customer-facing).

Recommended metrics (collect for QBR):
- Availability: uptime %, SLA compliance (monthly)
- Latency: p50/p90/p95 for generate and embeddings endpoints
- Errors: 4xx and 5xx rate and top error codes
- Throughput: requests per minute and tokens per minute
- Cost metrics: cost per 1k tokens, estimated monthly spend vs budget
- Quality: evaluation pass rate on customer prompt set, top regression examples
- Capacity: Dedicated GPU utilization and scaling events

QBR agenda template (60 minutes):
  1. Executive summary (5 min): adoption highlights and top outcomes.
  2. Operational health (15 min): uptime, L1/L2 incidents, latency and error trends.
  3. Quality & model performance (15 min): eval results, regressions, and recommended actions.
  4. Cost & optimization (10 min): opportunities for batching, quantization, or routing changes.
  5. Roadmap & requests (10 min): feature asks, upcoming releases.
  6. Action items and next steps (5 min): owners and due dates.

Artifacts to attach to QBR:
- Monthly usage and cost dashboard export (CSV/PDF)
- Top 10 prompts and sample outputs for quality discussion
- Incident review summaries since last QBR

8) Operational runbooks & quick commands
- Retrieve recent logs for request-id: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' 'https://logs.redwood.example.com/search?q=<REQUEST_ID>'
- Warm pool adjust (Dedicated CLI): redwood-dedicated scale --min-replicas 2 --region us-west-2
- Re-run eval prompt set: redwood-eval run --project <cust-id> --prompt-set qbr-core --output qbr-results.json

9) Related pages and appendices
- Link to Dedicated provisioning checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/dedicated-provisioning-2026
- On-call rota and SRE runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-rota-2025
- QBR slide template and speaker notes: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/qbr-templates-2026

Appendix A: Incident postmortem template (copyable)
- Title, Incident Window, Severity, Summary, Timeline, Root cause, Immediate mitigations, Long-term fixes, Owners & due dates, Customer communication log.

Appendix B: Onboarding checklist (copyable)
- API key created and validated (Y/N)
- Test traffic passed (Y/N)
- Observability hooks installed (Y/N)
- Cost alerts configured (Y/N)
- QBR date scheduled (Y/N)

Document maintenance
- Owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success).
- Review cadence: quarterly; reviewers: SE, SRE, Legal (if private deployments).
- Please link any updates to corresponding JIRA/incident for traceability.

End of playbook.
